Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.

  delete_unused_tags:

    command: "SolidQueue::Job.clear_finished_in_batches(sleep_between_batches: 0.3)"
    schedule: every hour at minute 12
  cleanup_webhook_deliveries:
    command: "Webhook::Delivery.cleanup"
    schedule: every 15 minutes
  cleanup_magic_links:
    command: "MagicLink.cleanup"
    schedule: every 4 hours
  cleanup_exports:
    command: "Export.cleanup"
    schedule: every hour at minute 20
  cleanup_imports:
    command: "Account::Import.cleanup"
    schedule: every hour at minute 25
  incineration:

  before_create :assign_number

  after_save   -> { board.touch }, if: :published?
  after_touch  -> { board.touch }, if: :published?
  after_update :handle_board_change, if: :saved_change_to_board_id?

  scope :indexed_by, ->(index) do
    case index
    when "stalled" then stalled
    when "postponing_soon" then postponing_soon
    when "closed" then closed
    when "maybe" then awaiting_triage
    when "not_now" then postponed.latest
    when "golden" then golden
    when "draft" then drafted
    else all
    end
  end

  scope :sorted_by, ->(sort) do
    case sort
    when "newest" then reverse_chronologically
    when "oldest" then chronologically
    when "latest" then latest
    else latest
    end
  end

  def card
    self
  end

  def to_param
    number.to_s
  end

  def move_to(new_board)
    transaction do
      card.update!(board: new_board)
      card.events.update_all(board_id: new_board.id)
      Event.where(eventable: card.comments).update_all(board_id: new_board.id)
    end
  end

  def filled?
    title.present? || description.present?
  end

  private

      self.title = "Untitled" if title.blank?
    end

      old_board = account.boards.find_by(id: board_id_before_last_save)

      transaction do
        update! column: nil
        track_board_change_event(old_board.name)
        grant_access_to_assignees unless board.all_access?

    def assign_number
      self.number ||= account.with_lock { account.increment!(:cards_count).cards_count }
    end

  attr_reader :card, :auto_clean_period

  class << self
    def for(card)
      return unless card.last_active_at

      new(card, card.auto_postpone_period)
    end
  end

  def initialize(card, auto_clean_period)
    @card = card
    @auto_clean_period = auto_clean_period
  end

  def auto_clean_at
    card.last_active_at + auto_clean_period
  end

    (auto_clean_period * 0.25).seconds.in_days.round
  end

  AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIODS_IN_DAYS = [ 3, 7, 30, 90, 365, 11 ].freeze
  AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIODS_IN_SECONDS = AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIODS_IN_DAYS.map { |n| n.day.in_seconds }.freeze

  belongs_to :container, polymorphic: true

  "output": "require "test_helper"

class Card::EntropicTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    Current.session = sessions(:david)
  end

  test "auto_postpone_at uses the period defined in the account by default" do
    freeze_time

    entropies(:writebook_board).destroy
    entropies("37s_account").reload.update! auto_postpone_period: 365.days
    cards(:layout).update! last_active_at: 2.day.ago
    assert_equal (365 - 2).days.from_now, cards(:layout).entropy.auto_clean_at
  end

  test "auto_postpone_at infers the period from the board when present" do
    freeze_time

    entropies(:writebook_board).update! auto_postpone_period: 90.days
    cards(:layout).update! last_active_at: 2.day.ago
    assert_equal (90 - 2).days.from_now, cards(:layout).entropy.auto_clean_at
  end

  test "setting auto_postpone_period in the board without entropy will create it, without affecting the account entropy" do
    account_entropy = entropies("37s_account")
    original_period = account_entropy.auto_postpone_period

    entropies(:writebook_board).destroy
    boards(:writebook).update! auto_postpone_period: 365.days

    assert_equal original_period, account_entropy.reload.auto_postpone_period
  end

  test "auto postpone all due using the default account entropy" do

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    scope :due_to_be_postponed, -> do
      active
        .joins(board: :account)
        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
        .where("last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', 'COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period)')}", Time.now)
    end

    scope :postponing_soon, -> do
      now = Time.now
      active
        .joins(board: :account)
        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
        .where("last_active_at > #{connection.date_subtract('?', 'COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period)')}", now)
        .where("last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', 'COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period) * 0.75')}", now)
    end

    delegate :auto_postpone_period, to: :board
  end

  class_methods do
    def auto_postpone_all_due
      due_to_be_postponed.find_each do |card|
        card.auto_postpone(user: card.account.system_user)

    end
  end

    entropy.present?

module Card::Statuses
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    enum :status, %w[ drafted published ].index_by(&:itself)

    before_save :mark_if_just_published
    after_create -> { track_event :published }, if: :published?
  end

  attr_accessor :was_just_published
  alias_method :was_just_published?, :was_just_published

  def publish
    transaction do
      self.created_at = Time.current
      published!
      track_event :published
    end
  end

  private
    def mark_if_just_published
      self.was_just_published = true if published? && status_changed?
    end
end

module Card::Postponable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :not_now, dependent: :destroy, class_name: "Card::NotNow"

    scope :postponed, -> { open.published.joins(:not_now) }
    scope :active, -> { open.published.where.missing(:not_now) }
  end

  def postponed?
    open? && published? && not_now.present?
  end

  def postponed_at
    not_now&.created_at
  end

  def postponed_by
    not_now&.user
  end

  def active?
    open? && published? && !postponed?
  end

module Card::Statuses
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    enum :status, %w[ drafted published ].index_by(&:itself)

    before_save :mark_if_just_published
    after_create -> { track_event :published }, if: :published?
  end

  attr_accessor :was_just_published
  alias_method :was_just_published?, :was_just_published

  def publish
    transaction do
      self.created_at = Time.current
      published!
      track_event :published
    end
  end

  private
    def mark_if_just_published
      self.was_just_published = true if published? && status_changed?
    end
end

module Card::Postponable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :not_now, dependent: :destroy, class_name: "Card::NotNow"

    scope :postponed, -> { open.published.joins(:not_now) }
    scope :active, -> { open.published.where.missing(:not_now) }
  end

  def postponed?
    open? && published? && not_now.present?
  end

  def postponed_at
    not_now&.created_at
  end

  def postponed_by
    not_now&.user
  end

  def active?
    open? && published? && !postponed?
  end

  def auto_postpone(**args)
    postpone(**args, event_name: :auto_postponed)
  end

  def postpone(user: Current.user, event_name: :postponed)
    transaction do
      send_back_to_triage(skip_event: true)
      reopen
      activity_spike&.destroy
      create_not_now!(user: user) unless postponed?
      track_event event_name, creator: user
    end
  end

  def resume
    transaction do
      reopen
      activity_spike&.destroy
      not_now&.destroy
    end
  end

# Adds database-agnostic date arithmetic methods to ActiveRecord adapters.
# This allows code to perform date calculations without checking which database adapter is in use.
#
# Usage:
#   connection.date_subtract("created_at", "3600")
#   # MySQL/Trilogy: "DATE_SUB(created_at, INTERVAL 3600 SECOND)"
#   # SQLite: "datetime(created_at, '-' || (3600) || ' seconds')"

# Module for MySQL-based adapters (Trilogy, Mysql2, etc.)
module MysqlDateArithmetic
  # Generates SQL for subtracting seconds from a date/time column in MySQL.
  #
  # @param date_column [String] The date/time column or expression
  # @param seconds_expression [String] SQL expression that evaluates to number of seconds
  # @return [String] MySQL DATE_SUB expression
  #
  # Example:
  #   date_subtract("last_active_at", "COALESCE(auto_postpone_period, 3600)")
  #   # => "DATE_SUB(last_active_at, INTERVAL COALESCE(auto_postpone_period, 3600) SECOND)"
  def date_subtract(date_column, seconds_expression)
    "DATE_SUB(#{date_column}, INTERVAL #{seconds_expression} SECOND)"
  end
end

# Module for SQLite adapter
module SqliteDateArithmetic
  # Generates SQL for subtracting seconds from a date/time column in SQLite.
  #
  # @param date_column [String] The date/time column or expression
  # @param seconds_expression [String] SQL expression that evaluates to number of seconds
  # @return [String] SQLite datetime expression
  #
  # Example:
  #   date_subtract("last_active_at", "COALESCE(auto_postpone_period, 3600)")
  #   # => "datetime(last_active_at, '-' || (COALESCE(auto_postpone_period, 3600)) || ' seconds')"
  def date_subtract(date_column, seconds_expression)
    "datetime(#{date_column}, '-' || (#{seconds_expression}) || ' seconds')"
  end
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
  # Prepend MySQL date arithmetic to AbstractMysqlAdapter (covers Trilogy, Mysql2, etc.)
  if defined?(ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::AbstractMysqlAdapter)
    ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::AbstractMysqlAdapter.prepend(MysqlDateArithmetic)
  end

  # Prepend SQLite date arithmetic to SQLite3Adapter
  if defined?(ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::SQLite3Adapter)
    ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::SQLite3Adapter.prepend(SqliteDateArithmetic)
  end
end

module Card::Closeable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :closure, dependent: :destroy

    scope :closed, -> { joins(:closure) }
    scope :open, -> { where.missing(:closure) }

    scope :recently_closed_first, -> { closed.order(closures: { created_at: :desc }) }
    scope :closed_at_window, ->(window) { closed.where(closures: { created_at: window }) }
    scope :closed_by, ->(users) { closed.where(closures: { user_id: Array(users) }) }
  end

  def closed?
    closure.present?
  end

  def open?
    !closed?
  end

  def closed_by
    closure&.user
  end

  def closed_at
    closure&.created_at
  end

  def close(user: Current.user)
    unless closed?
      transaction do
        not_now&.destroy
        create_closure! user: user
        track_event :closed, creator: user
      end
    end
  end

  def reopen(user: Current.user)
    if closed?
      transaction do
        closure&.destroy
        track_event :reopened, creator: user
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Adds database-agnostic date arithmetic methods to ActiveRecord adapters.
# This allows code to perform date calculations without checking which database adapter is in use.
#
# Usage:
#   connection.date_subtract("created_at", "3600")
#   # MySQL/Trilogy: "DATE_SUB(created_at, INTERVAL 3600 SECOND)"
#   # SQLite: "datetime(created_at, '-' || (3600) || ' seconds')"

# Module for MySQL-based adapters (Trilogy, Mysql2, etc.)
module MysqlDateArithmetic
  # Generates SQL for subtracting seconds from a date/time column in MySQL.
  #
  # @param date_column [String] The date/time column or expression
  # @param seconds_expression [String] SQL expression that evaluates to number of seconds
  # @return [String] MySQL DATE_SUB expression
  #
  # Example:
  #   date_subtract("last_active_at", "COALESCE(auto_postpone_period, 3600)")
  #   # => "DATE_SUB(last_active_at, INTERVAL COALESCE(auto_postpone_period, 3600) SECOND)"
  def date_subtract(date_column, seconds_expression)
    "DATE_SUB(#{date_column}, INTERVAL #{seconds_expression} SECOND)"
  end
end

# Module for SQLite adapter
module SqliteDateArithmetic
  # Generates SQL for subtracting seconds from a date/time column in SQLite.
  #
  # @param date_column [String] The date/time column or expression
  # @param seconds_expression [String] SQL expression that evaluates to number of seconds
  # @return [String] SQLite datetime expression
  #
  # Example:
  #   date_subtract("last_active_at", "COALESCE(auto_postpone_period, 3600)")
  #   # => "datetime(last_active_at, '-' || (COALESCE(auto_postpone_period, 3600)) || ' seconds')"
  def date_subtract(date_column, seconds_expression)
    "datetime(#{date_column}, '-' || (#{seconds_expression}) || ' seconds')"
  end
end

    ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::SQLite3Adapter.prepend(SqliteDateArithmetic)

module Card::Closeable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :closure, dependent: :destroy

    scope :closed, -> { joins(:closure) }
    scope :open, -> { where.missing(:closure) }

    scope :recently_closed_first, -> { closed.order(closures: { created_at: :desc }) }
    scope :closed_at_window, ->(window) { closed.where(closures: { created_at: window }) }
    scope :closed_by, ->(users) { closed.where(closures: { user_id: Array(users) }) }
  end

  def closed?
    closure.present?
  end

  def open?
    !closed?
  end

  def closed_by
    closure&.user
  end

  def closed_at
    closure&.created_at
  end

  def close(user: Current.user)
    unless closed?
      transaction do
        not_now&.destroy
        create_closure! user: user
        track_event :closed, creator: user
      end
    end
  end

  def reopen(user: Current.user)
    if closed?
      transaction do
        closure&.destroy
        track_event :reopened, creator: user
      end
    end
  end
end

class NotificationsDataMigration < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.2]
  BATCH_SIZE = 10_000

  class Notification < ActiveRecord::Base
    self.table_name = "notifications"
  end

  def change
    reversible do |dir|
      dir.up do
        populate_card_id
        collapse_duplicates
      end
    end

    change_column_null :notifications, :card_id, false
    add_index :notifications, [ :user_id, :card_id ], unique: true
  end

  private
    def populate_card_id
      execute(<<~SQL)
        UPDATE notifications
        SET card_id = (
          SELECT CASE events.eventable_type
            WHEN 'Card' THEN events.eventable_id
            WHEN 'Comment' THEN (SELECT comments.card_id FROM comments WHERE comments.id = events.eventable_id)
          END
          FROM events
          WHERE events.id = notifications.source_id
        )
        WHERE notifications.card_id IS NULL
          AND notifications.source_type = 'Event'
      SQL

      execute(<<~SQL)
        UPDATE notifications
        SET card_id = (
          SELECT CASE mentions.source_type
            WHEN 'Card' THEN mentions.source_id
            WHEN 'Comment' THEN (SELECT comments.card_id FROM comments WHERE comments.id = mentions.source_id)
          END
          FROM mentions
          WHERE mentions.id = notifications.source_id
        )
        WHERE notifications.card_id IS NULL
          AND notifications.source_type = 'Mention'
      SQL
    end

    def collapse_duplicates
      loop do
        duplicates = Notification.find_by_sql(<<~SQL)
          SELECT user_id, card_id,
                 MAX(id) AS keep_id,
                 COUNT(*) AS total,
                 SUM(CASE WHEN read_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unread_total
          FROM notifications
          WHERE card_id IS NOT NULL
          GROUP BY user_id, card_id
          HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
          LIMIT #{BATCH_SIZE}
        SQL

        break if duplicates.empty?

        duplicates.each do |row|
          Notification.where(user_id: row.user_id, card_id: row.card_id)
            .where.not(id: row.keep_id)
            .delete_all

          Notification.where(id: row.keep_id)
            .update_all(unread_count: row.unread_total.to_i)
        end
      end

      # Set unread_count for remaining non-collapsed notifications
      execute(<<~SQL)
        UPDATE notifications
        SET unread_count = CASE WHEN read_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        WHERE unread_count = 0 AND card_id IS NOT NULL
      SQL
    end
end

messages.content: A simple index alone won’t make the dynamic period comparison fully searchable: the cutoff is derived from a joined board/account row.     VALUES ('0000000000000000000000004', '#{account_id}', 'Account', '#{account_id}', #{365.days.to_i}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
  SQL
  connection.execute(<<~SQL)

      VALUES (1)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < 100000
    )

require "benchmark"

connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
account_id = "0000000000000000000000001"
board_id = "0000000000000000000000002"
creator_id = "0000000000000000000000003"
period = 365.days.to_i

connection.transaction do
  connection.execute(<<~SQL)
    INSERT INTO accounts (id, name, cards_count, created_at, updated_at)
    VALUES ('#{account_id}', 'Benchmark account', 100000, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
  SQL
  connection.execute(<<~SQL)
    INSERT INTO boards (id, account_id, creator_id, name, all_access, created_at, updated_at)
    VALUES ('#{board_id}', '#{account_id}', '#{creator_id}', 'Benchmark board', 1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
  SQL
  connection.execute(<<~SQL)
    INSERT INTO entropies (id, account_id, container_type, container_id, auto_postpone_period, created_at, updated_at)
    VALUES ('0000000000000000000000004', '#{account_id}', 'Account', '#{account_id}', #{period}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
  SQL
  connection.execute(<<~SQL)
    WITH RECURSIVE sequence(number) AS (
      VALUES (1)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < 100000
    )
    INSERT INTO cards (id, account_id, board_id, creator_id, number, status, last_active_at, created_at, updated_at)
    SELECT printf('%025d', number), '#{account_id}', '#{board_id}', '#{creator_id}', number,
           'published',
           CASE WHEN number % 10 = 0
             THEN datetime('now', '-' || (370 + (number % 30)) || ' days')
             ELSE datetime('now', '-' || ((number % 90) + 1) || ' days')
           END,
           CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
    FROM sequence
  SQL
end

messages.content: Now the baseline is repeatable: 100,000 records, 10,000 due, current plan `SCAN cards`, and cold/warm candidate-loading times of about 0.067–0.107 seconds. I’ll compare the exact current selector with a period-specific candidate selector on the same throwaway DB, first without and then with each plausible index order. This will show whether the added range actually changes SQLite’s plan and runtime.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/entropy_compare_indexes.rb
require "benchmark"

connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
now = Time.now
period = 365.days.to_i
period_sql = "COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period)"
base = Card.active
  .joins(board: :account)
  .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
  .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
candidate = base
  .where("#{period_sql} = ?", period)
  .where(cards: { last_active_at: ..(now - period) })
  .where("cards.last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', period_sql)}", now)

puts "current_count=#{Card.due_to_be_postponed.count} candidate_count=#{candidate.count}"
puts "current_plan:"
puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{Card.due_to_be_postponed.to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
puts "candidate_plan_without_extra_index:"
puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{candidate.to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }

[
  ["last_active_at", "status"],
  ["status", "last_active_at"]
].each do |columns|
  connection.execute("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS benchmark_cards_by_date_and_status")
  connection.add_index(:cards, columns, name: "benchmark_cards_by_date_and_status")
  puts "candidate_plan_with_#{columns.join('_')}_index:"
  puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{candidate.to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
  3.times do
    elapsed = Benchmark.realtime { Card.uncached { candidate.load } }
    puts "index=#{columns.join('_')} load_seconds=#{elapsed.round(4)} loaded=#{candidate.size}"
  end
end
connection.execute("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS benchmark_cards_by_date_and_status")
EOF

AND last_active_at<?)` when given an index with status/date order. I’m now checking the plan for Rails’ actual keyset-batched `find_each` queries, since that is how the recurring job executes the scope.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/entropy_benchmark_batches.rb
require "benchmark"

connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
now = Time.now
period = 365.days.to_i
period_sql = "COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period)"
base = Card.due_to_be_postponed
candidate = base
  .where("#{period_sql} = ?", period)
  .where(cards: { last_active_at: ..(now - period) })

connection.add_index(:cards, [ :status, :last_active_at ], name: "benchmark_cards_by_status_and_date")
[ [ "current", base ], [ "period-filtered", candidate ] ].each do |name, relation|
  puts "#{name} count=#{relation.count}"
  [ nil, "0000000000000000000000000" ].each do |last_id|
    page = relation
    page = page.where("cards.id > ?", last_id) if last_id
    page = page.order(id: :asc).limit(1001)
    puts "#{name} plan last_id=#{last_id || 'nil'}:"
    puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{page.to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
  end
  3.times do
    count = 0
    queries = 0
    subscriber = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("sql.active_record") do |_event, _start, _finish, _id, payload|
      queries += 1 if payload[:sql].start_with?("SELECT \"cards\".*") && !payload[:cached]
    end
    elapsed = Benchmark.realtime do
      Card.uncached do
        relation.find_each { count += 1 }
      end
    end
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(subscriber)
    puts "#{name} find_each_seconds=#{elapsed.round(4)} loaded=#{count} card_selects=#{queries}"
  end
end
connection.remove_index(:cards, name: "benchmark_cards_by_status_and_date")
EOF

module ActiveRecord
  module Type
    class Uuid < Binary
      BASE36_LENGTH = 25 # 36^25 > 2^128

      class << self
        def generate
          uuid = SecureRandom.uuid_v7
          hex = uuid.delete("-")
          hex_to_base36(hex)
        end

        def hex_to_base36(hex)
          hex.to_i(16).to_s(36).rjust(BASE36_LENGTH, "0")
        end

        def base36_to_hex(base36)
          base36.to_s.to_i(36).to_s(16).rjust(32, "0")
        end
      end

      def serialize(value)
        return unless value

        binary = Uuid.base36_to_hex(value).scan(/../).map(&:hex).pack("C*")
        super(binary)
      end

      def deserialize(value)
        return unless value

        hex = value.to_s.unpack1("H*")
        Uuid.hex_to_base36(hex)
      end

      def cast(value)
        value
      end
    end
  end
end

      active

connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
account_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
board_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
creator_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
now = Time.current
period = 365.days.to_i

Account.insert_all!([{ id: account_id, name: "Benchmark account", external_account_id: 900001, cards_count: 100000, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Board.insert_all!([{ id: board_id, account_id: account_id, creator_id: creator_id, name: "Benchmark board", all_access: true, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Entropy.insert_all!([{ id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Account", container_id: account_id, auto_postpone_period: period, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
connection.execute(<<~SQL)
  WITH RECURSIVE sequence(number) AS (
    VALUES (1)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < 100000
  )
  INSERT INTO cards (id, account_id, board_id, creator_id, number, status, last_active_at, created_at, updated_at)
  SELECT randomblob(16), #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(account_id))},
         #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(board_id))},
         #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(creator_id))}, number,
         'published',
         CASE WHEN number % 10 = 0
           THEN datetime('now', '-' || (370 + (number % 30)) || ' days')
           ELSE datetime('now', '-' || ((number % 90) + 1) || ' days')
         END,
         CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  FROM sequence
SQL

expected = Card.due_to_be_postponed.count
periods = Entropy.distinct.pluck(:auto_postpone_period)
puts "cards=#{Card.count} distinct_periods=#{periods.inspect} expected_due=#{expected}"
periods.each do |period_value|
  relation = Card.due_to_be_postponed(now)
    .where("#{Card::Entropic::EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL} = ?", period_value)
    .where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", now - period_value)
  puts "period=#{period_value} due=#{relation.count} plan:"
  puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{relation.order(:id).limit(1001).to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
end
3.times do
  count = 0
  selects = 0
  subscriber = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("sql.active_record") do |_event, _start, _finish, _id, payload|
    selects += 1 if payload[:sql].start_with?("SELECT \"cards\".*") && !payload[:cached]
  end
  elapsed = Benchmark.realtime do
    Card.uncached do
      Entropy.distinct.pluck(:auto_postpone_period).each do |period_value|
        Card.due_to_be_postponed(now)
          .where("#{Card::Entropic::EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL} = ?", period_value)
          .where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", now - period_value)
          .find_each(batch_size: 1000) { count += 1 }
      end
    end
  end
  ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(subscriber)
  puts "optimized_find_each_seconds=#{elapsed.round(4)} loaded=#{count} card_selects=#{selects}"
end
raise "optimized selector returned wrong count: #{expected} != #{count}" unless count == expected
EOF

require "benchmark"

connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
connection.execute("DELETE FROM cards")
connection.execute("DELETE FROM entropies")
connection.execute("DELETE FROM boards")
connection.execute("DELETE FROM accounts")
account_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
board_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
creator_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
now = Time.current
period = 365.days.to_i
Account.insert_all!([{ id: account_id, name: "Benchmark account", external_account_id: 900001, cards_count: 100000, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Board.insert_all!([{ id: board_id, account_id: account_id, creator_id: creator_id, name: "Benchmark board", all_access: true, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Entropy.insert_all!([{ id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Account", container_id: account_id, auto_postpone_period: period, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
connection.execute(<<~SQL)
  WITH RECURSIVE sequence(number) AS (
    VALUES (1)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < 100000
  )
  INSERT INTO cards (id, account_id, board_id, creator_id, number, status, last_active_at, created_at, updated_at)
  SELECT randomblob(16), #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(account_id))},
         #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(board_id))},
         #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(creator_id))}, number,
         'published',
         CASE WHEN number % 10 = 0
           THEN datetime('now', '-' || (370 + (number % 30)) || ' days')
           ELSE datetime('now', '-' || ((number % 90) + 1) || ' days')
         END,
         CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  FROM sequence
SQL

periods = Entropy.distinct.pluck(:auto_postpone_period)
period_sql = Card::Entropic::EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL
base = Card.due_to_be_postponed(now)
per_period = periods.map do |period_value|
  base.where("#{period_sql} = ?", period_value).where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", now - period_value)
end
or_sql = periods.map { "(#{period_sql} = ? AND cards.last_active_at <= ?)" }.join(" OR ")
args = periods.flat_map { |period_value| [ period_value, now - period_value ] }
combined = base.where("(#{or_sql})", *args)

variants = {
  "per-period/default-cursor" => [ -> { per_period }, { batch_size: 1000 } ],
  "per-period/date-cursor" => [ -> { per_period }, { batch_size: 1000, cursor: [ :last_active_at, :id ], order: [ :asc, :asc ] } ],
  "combined/default-cursor" => [ -> { [ combined ] }, { batch_size: 1000 } ],
  "combined/date-cursor" => [ -> { [ combined ] }, { batch_size: 1000, cursor: [ :last_active_at, :id ], order: [ :asc, :asc ] } ]
}
puts "cards=#{Card.count} periods=#{periods.inspect} expected=#{base.count}"
variants.each do |name, (relations, options)|
  first_relation = relations.call.first
  page = first_relation.order(options[:cursor] ? { last_active_at: :asc, id: :asc } : { id: :asc }).limit(1001)
  puts "#{name} plan:"
  puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{page.to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
  3.times do
    loaded = 0
    count = 0
    elapsed = Benchmark.realtime do
      Card.uncached do
        relations.call.each do |relation|
          relation.find_each(**options) { count += 1 }
        end
      end
    end
    loaded = count
    puts "#{name} seconds=#{elapsed.round(4)} loaded=#{loaded}"
  end
end
EOF

messages.content: The single-period fixture showed that batching per period can erase the benefit when several periods are configured. A better candidate is one SQL query containing the disjoint `(effective_period = P AND last_active_at <= now-P)` ranges, which avoids repeated scans and preserves the fixed-run timestamp. I’ll benchmark that against the per-period loop on 100,000 cards spread across all six supported periods.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/entropy_benchmark_six_periods.rb
require "benchmark"

connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
[ :cards, :entropies, :boards, :accounts ].each { |table| connection.execute("DELETE FROM #{table}") }
account_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
creator_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
now = Time.current
periods_in_days = [ 3, 7, 11, 30, 90, 365 ]
periods = periods_in_days.map { |days| days.days.to_i }
account_entropy_period = 30.days.to_i
Account.insert_all!([{ id: account_id, name: "Benchmark account", external_account_id: 900001, cards_count: 100000, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Entropy.insert_all!([{ id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Account", container_id: account_id, auto_postpone_period: account_entropy_period, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
board_ids = periods.map { ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate }
Board.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map do |board_id, index|
  { id: board_id, account_id: account_id, creator_id: creator_id, name: "Board #{index}", all_access: true, created_at: now, updated_at: now }
end)
Entropy.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map do |board_id, index|
  { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Board", container_id: board_id, auto_postpone_period: periods[index], created_at: now, updated_at: now }
end)
board_sql = board_ids.map { |id| connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(id)) }
board_case = board_sql.each_with_index.map { |id, index| "WHEN #{index} THEN #{id}" }.join(" ")
period_case = periods.each_with_index.map { |period, index| "WHEN #{index} THEN #{period}" }.join(" ")
connection.execute(<<~SQL)
  WITH RECURSIVE sequence(number) AS (
    VALUES (1)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < 100000
  )
  INSERT INTO cards (id, account_id, board_id, creator_id, number, status, last_active_at, created_at, updated_at)
  SELECT randomblob(16), #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(account_id))},
         CASE number % 6 #{board_case} END,
         #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(creator_id))}, number,
         'published',
         CASE WHEN number % 10 = 0
           THEN datetime('now', '-' || ((CASE number % 6 #{period_case} END) / 86400 + 5) || ' days')
           ELSE datetime('now', '-' || ((number % 2) + 1) || ' days')
         END,
         CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  FROM sequence
SQL

base = Card.due_to_be_postponed(now)
current_periods = Entropy.distinct.pluck(:auto_postpone_period)
period_sql = Card::Entropic::EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL
parts = current_periods.map { "(#{period_sql} = ? AND cards.last_active_at <= ?)" }.join(" OR ")
binds = current_periods.flat_map { |period| [ period, now - period ] }
combined = base.where("(#{parts})", *binds)
per_period = current_periods.map do |period|
  base.where("#{period_sql} = ?", period).where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", now - period)
end
puts "cards=#{Card.count} periods=#{current_periods.inspect} expected_due=#{base.count} combined_due=#{combined.count}"
[ [ "baseline", [ base ] ], [ "per-period", per_period ], [ "combined-or", [ combined ] ] ].each do |name, relations|
  first = relations.first
  puts "#{name} plan:"
  puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{first.order(:id).limit(1001).to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
  3.times do
    count = 0
    elapsed = Benchmark.realtime do
      Card.uncached do
        relations.each do |relation|
          relation.find_each(batch_size: 1000) { count += 1 }
        end
      end
    end
    puts "#{name}_seconds=#{elapsed.round(4)} loaded=#{count}"
  end
end
raise "combined candidate mismatch" unless combined.pluck(:id).sort == base.pluck(:id).sort
EOF

messages.content: The data confirms a simpler, safer strategy: one prefilter at the minimum entropy period present in the database. Every effective card period is either a board entropy row or an account entropy row, so the persisted minimum is a conservative lower bound; the existing exact due predicate still decides eligibility. I’ll replace the repeated per-period queries with one indexed range, padding the cutoff by one second to avoid excluding cards at SQLite’s second-precision boundary.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > app/models/card/entropic.rb
module Card::Entropic
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL = "COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period)".freeze

  included do
    scope :due_to_be_postponed, ->(now = Time.now) do
      active
        .joins(board: :account)
        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
        .where("cards.last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL)}", now)
    end

    scope :postponing_soon, -> do
      now = Time.now
      active
        .joins(board: :account)
        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
        .where("cards.last_active_at > #{connection.date_subtract('?', EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL)}", now)
        .where("cards.last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', "#{EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL} * 0.75")}", now)
    end

    delegate :auto_postpone_period, to: :board
  end

  class_methods do
    def auto_postpone_all_due
      now = Time.now
      minimum_period = Entropy.minimum(:auto_postpone_period)

      if minimum_period
        due_to_be_postponed(now)
          .where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", now - minimum_period + 1.second)
          .find_each do |card|
            card.auto_postpone(user: card.account.system_user)
          end
      end
    end
  end

  def entropy
    Card::Entropy.for(self)
  end

  def entropic?
    entropy.present?
  end
end
EOF

messages.content: The all-period regression still passes after switching to one minimum-period range. I’ll measure this exact approach now against the original unbounded query on 500,000 synthetic cards with six board entropy periods, checking that it selects exactly the same due-card IDs and uses the new range index.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/entropy_benchmark_min_period.rb
require "benchmark"

connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
card_count = Integer(ENV.fetch("CARD_COUNT", "500000"))
[ :cards, :entropies, :boards, :accounts ].each { |table| connection.execute("DELETE FROM #{table}") }
account_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
creator_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
now = Time.current
periods = [ 3, 7, 11, 30, 90, 365 ].map { |days| days.days.to_i }
Account.insert_all!([{ id: account_id, name: "Benchmark account", external_account_id: 900001, cards_count: card_count, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Entropy.insert_all!([{ id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Account", container_id: account_id, auto_postpone_period: 30.days.to_i, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
board_ids = periods.map { ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate }
Board.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: id, account_id: account_id, creator_id: creator_id, name: "Board #{i}", all_access: true, created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
Entropy.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Board", container_id: id, auto_postpone_period: periods[i], created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
board_sql = board_ids.map { |id| connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(id)) }
board_case = board_sql.each_with_index.map { |id, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{id}" }.join(" ")
period_case = periods.each_with_index.map { |period, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{period}" }.join(" ")
connection.execute(<<~SQL)
  WITH RECURSIVE sequence(number) AS (
    VALUES (1)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < #{card_count}
  )
  INSERT INTO cards (id, account_id, board_id, creator_id, number, status, last_active_at, created_at, updated_at)
  SELECT randomblob(16), #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(account_id))},
         CASE number % 6 #{board_case} END, #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(creator_id))}, number, 'published',
         CASE WHEN number % 10 = 0 THEN datetime('now', '-' || ((CASE number % 6 #{period_case} END) / 86400 + 5) || ' days')
              ELSE datetime('now', '-' || ((number % 2) + 1) || ' days') END,
         CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  FROM sequence
SQL
base = Card.due_to_be_postponed(now)
expected_ids = base.pluck(:id).to_set
minimum_period = Entropy.minimum(:auto_postpone_period)
optimized = base.where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", now - minimum_period + 1.second)
actual_ids = optimized.pluck(:id).to_set
raise "candidate mismatch: missing=#{(expected_ids - actual_ids).size} extra=#{(actual_ids - expected_ids).size}" unless actual_ids == expected_ids
puts "cards=#{Card.count} due=#{expected_ids.size} entropy_periods=#{Entropy.distinct.pluck(:auto_postpone_period).size} minimum_period=#{minimum_period} ids_match=true"

connection.remove_index(:cards, name: "index_cards_on_status_and_last_active_at")
puts "baseline_plan:"
puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{base.order(:id).limit(1001).to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
3.times do
  count = 0
  seconds = Benchmark.realtime { Card.uncached { base.find_each(batch_size: 1000) { count += 1 } } }
  puts "baseline_seconds=#{seconds.round(4)} loaded=#{count}"
end
connection.add_index(:cards, [ :status, :last_active_at ], name: "index_cards_on_status_and_last_active_at")
puts "optimized_plan:"
puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{optimized.order(:id).limit(1001).to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
3.times do
  count = 0
  seconds = Benchmark.realtime { Card.uncached { optimized.find_each(batch_size: 1000) { count += 1 } } }
  puts "optimized_seconds=#{seconds.round(4)} loaded=#{count}"
end
EOF

messages.content: The 500,000-card benchmark uncovered a regression in SQLite’s ordering cost: the minimum-date range reduced candidates from 500,000 to 50,000, but primary-key `find_each` had to sort those candidates, making the run ~1.9s versus ~0.67s for the original ID-ordered scan. I’ll test a `(status, last_active_at, id)` index with matching date/ID keyset order, which should avoid that sort; if it doesn’t, we need another strategy.

messages.content: The job’s postponed cards are removed from the `active` scope as soon as the action runs. Rails computes each batch’s cursor values before yielding that batch, so an ascending `(last_active_at, id)` cursor can safely use the range index even though postponing updates `last_active_at`. I’ll test this cursor at 1%-due scale, where avoiding a full scan should have the clearest payoff.

            card.auto_postpone(user: card.account.system_user)
          end
      end

module Card::Commentable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy
  end

  def commentable?
    published?
  end

  private
    STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE = 1000

    # Override to include comments, but only load comments that have attachments.
    # Cards can have thousands of comments; most won't have attachments.
    # Streams in batches to avoid loading all IDs into memory at once.
    def storage_transfer_records
      comment_ids_with_attachments = storage_comment_ids_with_attachments

      if comment_ids_with_attachments.any?
        [ self, *comments.where(id: comment_ids_with_attachments).to_a ]
      else
        [ self ]
      end
    end

    def storage_comment_ids_with_attachments
      direct = []
      rich_text_map = {}

      # Stream comment IDs in batches to avoid loading all into memory
      comments.in_batches(of: STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE) do |batch|
        batch_ids = batch.pluck(:id)

        direct.concat \
          ActiveStorage::Attachment
            .where(record_type: "Comment", record_id: batch_ids)
            .distinct
            .pluck(:record_id)

        ActionText::RichText
          .where(record_type: "Comment", record_id: batch_ids)
          .pluck(:id, :record_id)
          .each { |rt_id, comment_id| rich_text_map[rt_id] = comment_id }
      end

      embed_comment_ids = if rich_text_map.any?
        rich_text_map.keys.each_slice(STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE).flat_map do |batch_ids|
          ActiveStorage::Attachment
            .where(record_type: "ActionText::RichText", record_id: batch_ids)
            .distinct
            .pluck(:record_id)
        end.filter_map { |rt_id| rich_text_map[rt_id] }
      else
        []
      end

      (direct + embed_comment_ids).uniq
    end
end
"
}

messages.content: Before finalizing the cutoff, I’m checking a common configuration where no account or board uses the three-day option (the shortest persisted period is 30 days). A global three-day lower bound may be safe but needlessly broad; the persisted minimum is enough for the current sweep’s exact joined predicate, and should let the index skip more records. I’ll benchmark both bounds on the same 500,000-card fixture.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/entropy_benchmark_bounds.rb
require "benchmark"
connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
card_count = 500000
[ :cards, :entropies, :boards, :accounts ].each { |table| connection.execute("DELETE FROM #{table}") }
account_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
creator_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
now = Time.current
periods = [ 30, 90, 365 ].map { |days| days.days.to_i }
Account.insert_all!([{ id: account_id, name: "Benchmark account", external_account_id: 990002, cards_count: card_count, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Entropy.insert_all!([{ id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Account", container_id: account_id, auto_postpone_period: periods[0], created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
board_ids = periods.map { ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate }
Board.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: id, account_id: account_id, creator_id: creator_id, name: "Board #{i}", all_access: true, created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
Entropy.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Board", container_id: id, auto_postpone_period: periods[i], created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
board_sql = board_ids.map { |id| connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(id)) }
board_case = board_sql.each_with_index.map { |id, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{id}" }.join(" ")
connection.execute(<<~SQL)
  WITH RECURSIVE sequence(number) AS (VALUES (1) UNION ALL SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < #{card_count})
  INSERT INTO cards (id, account_id, board_id, creator_id, number, status, last_active_at, created_at, updated_at)
  SELECT randomblob(16), #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(account_id))},
         CASE number % 3 #{board_case} END, #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(creator_id))}, number, 'published',
         CASE WHEN number % 100 = 0
           THEN datetime('now', '-' || (CASE number % 3 WHEN 0 THEN 35 WHEN 1 THEN 95 ELSE 370 END) || ' days')
           ELSE datetime('now', '-' || ((number % 60) + 1) || ' days') END,
         CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  FROM sequence
SQL
base = Card.due_to_be_postponed(now)
min_period = Entropy.minimum(:auto_postpone_period)
expected = base.pluck(:id).to_set
puts "cards=#{Card.count} due=#{expected.size} persisted_min_days=#{min_period / 86400}"
connection.remove_index(:cards, name: "index_cards_on_status_and_last_active_at_and_id")
3.times do
  count = 0
  seconds = Benchmark.realtime { Card.uncached { base.find_each(batch_size: 1000) { count += 1 } } }
  puts "baseline_seconds=#{seconds.round(4)} loaded=#{count}"
end
connection.add_index(:cards, [ :status, :last_active_at, :id ], name: "index_cards_on_status_and_last_active_at_and_id")
[ [ "allowed_min", Entropy::AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIODS_IN_SECONDS.min ], [ "persisted_min", min_period ] ].each do |name, cutoff_period|
  relation = base.where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", now - cutoff_period + 1.second)
  ids = relation.pluck(:id).to_set

messages.content: The benchmark confirmed the trade-off: the globally supported minimum is safest, but if no account actually uses the three-day option it widens the indexed range unnecessarily. Since entropy rows are updated before the sweep query and the per-card exact predicate remains authoritative, I’ll use the minimum persisted entropy period, while retaining a defensive fallback to the allowed minimum when the table is empty. Then I’ll rerun the full suite and final checks.The measurement confirms that a fixed three-day prefilter can be too broad for 30/90/365-day accounts. I’ll use the minimum currently persisted period (with the allowed minimum only as a no-entropy fallback) and make the sweep adaptive: count the simple indexed candidates first, use date-order batching only when that set is selective, otherwise keep the original ID-ordered sweep. I’ll measure both branches before finalizing this guard.

messages.content: My temporary benchmark-edit script failed while building its SQL-string replacement, so it reran the prior hybrid benchmark instead; those results add no new evidence. I’ll write a simpler standalone script from scratch to compare unbounded versus bounded descending-date cursors without modifying repository code.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/entropy_cursor_compare.rb
require "benchmark"
connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
card_count = 500000
mode = ENV.fetch("MODE", "sparse")
[ :cards, :entropies, :boards, :accounts ].each { |table| connection.execute("DELETE FROM #{table}") }
account_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
creator_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
now = Time.current
periods = (mode == "sparse" ? [ 3, 7, 11, 30, 90, 365 ] : [ 30, 90, 365 ]).map { |days| days.days.to_i }
Account.insert_all!([{ id: account_id, name: "Cursor benchmark", external_account_id: mode == "sparse" ? 990006 : 990007, cards_count: card_count, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Entropy.insert_all!([{ id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Account", container_id: account_id, auto_postpone_period: periods.min, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
board_ids = periods.map { ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate }
Board.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: id, account_id: account_id, creator_id: creator_id, name: "Board #{i}", all_access: true, created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
Entropy.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Board", container_id: id, auto_postpone_period: periods[i], created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
board_sql = board_ids.map { |id| connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(id)) }
board_case = board_sql.each_with_index.map { |id, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{id}" }.join(" ")
period_case = periods.each_with_index.map { |period, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{period}" }.join(" ")
non_due_days = mode == "sparse" ? "((number % 2) + 1)" : "((number % 60) + 1)"
connection.execute(<<~SQL)
  WITH RECURSIVE sequence(number) AS (VALUES (1) UNION ALL SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < #{card_count})
  INSERT INTO cards (id, account_id, board_id, creator_id, number, status, last_active_at, created_at, updated_at)
  SELECT randomblob(16), #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(account_id))},
         CASE number % #{periods.size} #{board_case} END,
         #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(creator_id))}, number, 'published',
         CASE WHEN number % 100 = 0
           THEN datetime('now', '-' || ((CASE number % #{periods.size} #{period_case} END) / 86400 + 5) || ' days')
           ELSE datetime('now', '-' || #{non_due_days} || ' days') END,
         CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  FROM sequence
SQL
base = Card.due_to_be_postponed(now)
minimum_period = [ Entropy::AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIODS_IN_SECONDS.min, Entropy.minimum(:auto_postpone_period) ].compact.min
cutoff = now - minimum_period + 1.second
bounded = base.where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", cutoff)
puts "mode=#{mode} cards=#{Card.count} due=#{base.count} periods=#{periods.size}"
[ [ "id-order", base, { cursor: :id, order: :asc } ],
  [ "full-date-order", base, { cursor: [ :last_active_at, :id ], order: [ :desc, :desc ] } ],
  [ "bounded-date-order", bounded, { cursor: [ :last_active_at, :id ], order: [ :desc, :desc ] } ] ].each do |label, relation, options|
  page = relation.reorder(options[:cursor] == :id ? { id: :asc } : { last_active_at: :desc, id: :desc }).limit(1001)
  puts "#{label}_plan:"
  puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{page.to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
  3.times do
    count = 0
    seconds = Benchmark.realtime do
      Card.uncached do
        relation.find_each(batch_size: 1000, **options) { count += 1 }
      end
    end
    puts "#{label}_seconds=#{seconds.round(4)} loaded=#{count}"
  end
end
EOF
for mode in sparse dense; do cp storage/test.sqlite3 "/tmp/fizzy-entropy-cursor-${mode}.sqlite3"; MODE="$mode" RAILS_ENV=test DATABASE_URL="sqlite3:/tmp/fizzy-entropy-cursor-${mode}.sqlite3" bundle exec rails runner /tmp/entropy_cursor_compare.rb || exit $?; rm -f "/tmp/fizzy-entropy-cursor-${mode}.sqlite3"; done

module Card::Entropic
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL = "COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period)".freeze
  DATE_RANGE_SELECTIVITY_DENOMINATOR = 10

  included do
    scope :due_to_be_postponed, ->(now = Time.now) do
      active
        .joins(board: :account)
        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
        .where("cards.last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL)}", now)
    end

    scope :postponing_soon, -> do
      now = Time.now
      active
        .joins(board: :account)
        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
        .where("cards.last_active_at > #{connection.date_subtract('?', EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL)}", now)
        .where("cards.last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', "#{EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL} * 0.75")}", now)
    end

    delegate :auto_postpone_period, to: :board
  end

  class_methods do
    def auto_postpone_all_due
      now = Time.now
      minimum_period = [
        Entropy::AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIODS_IN_SECONDS.min,
        Entropy.minimum(:auto_postpone_period)
      ].compact.min
      date_cutoff = now - minimum_period + 1.second
      published_cards = published
      date_range_candidate_count = published_cards.where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", date_cutoff).count
      published_card_count = published_cards.count
      due_cards = due_to_be_postponed(now)

      if date_range_candidate_count * DATE_RANGE_SELECTIVITY_DENOMINATOR < published_card_count
        # SQLite's datetime() drops fractional seconds, so keep the date prefilter one second wider.
        due_cards = due_cards.where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", date_cutoff)
          # Auto-postponing advances last_active_at, so descending order keeps changed cards behind the cursor.
          .find_each(cursor: [ :last_active_at, :id ], order: [ :desc, :desc ]) do |card|
            card.auto_postpone(user: card.account.system_user)
          end
      else
        due_cards.find_each do |card|
          card.auto_postpone(user: card.account.system_user)
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def entropy
    Card::Entropy.for(self)
  end

  def entropic?
    entropy.present?
  end
end

The sparse case should take the range-index path; the dense case should keep the original ID path, with the date-leading index not disturbing that plan.

require "benchmark"

connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
card_count = 500000
mode = ENV.fetch("MODE", "sparse")
[ :cards, :entropies, :boards, :accounts ].each { |table| connection.execute("DELETE FROM #{table}") }
connection.remove_index(:cards, name: "index_cards_on_status_and_last_active_at_and_id")
connection.add_index(:cards, [ :last_active_at, :id, :status ], name: "index_cards_on_last_active_at_and_id_and_status")
account_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
creator_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
now = Time.current
periods = (mode == "sparse" ? [ 3, 7, 11, 30, 90, 365 ] : [ 30, 90, 365 ]).map { |days| days.days.to_i }
Account.insert_all!([{ id: account_id, name: "Benchmark account", external_account_id: (mode == "sparse" ? 990008 : 990009), cards_count: card_count, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
Entropy.insert_all!([{ id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Account", container_id: account_id, auto_postpone_period: periods.min, created_at: now, updated_at: now }])
board_ids = periods.map { ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate }
Board.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: id, account_id: account_id, creator_id: creator_id, name: "Board #{i}", all_access: true, created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
Entropy.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Board", container_id: id, auto_postpone_period: periods[i], created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
board_sql = board_ids.map { |id| connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(id)) }
board_case = board_sql.each_with_index.map { |id, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{id}" }.join(" ")
period_case = periods.each_with_index.map { |period, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{period}" }.join(" ")
non_due_days = mode == "sparse" ? "((number % 2) + 1)" : "((number % 60) + 1)"
connection.execute(<<~SQL)
  WITH RECURSIVE sequence(number) AS (VALUES (1) UNION ALL SELECT number + 1 FROM sequence WHERE number < #{card_count})
  INSERT INTO cards (id, account_id, board_id, creator_id, number, status, last_active_at, created_at, updated_at)
  SELECT randomblob(16), #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(account_id))},
         CASE number % #{periods.size} #{board_case} END,
         #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(creator_id))}, number, 'published',
         CASE WHEN number % 100 = 0
           THEN datetime('now', '-' || ((CASE number % #{periods.size} #{period_case} END) / 86400 + 5) || ' days')
           ELSE datetime('now', '-' || #{non_due_days} || ' days') END,
         CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  FROM sequence
SQL
base = Card.due_to_be_postponed(now)
published = Card.published
minimum_period = Entropy.minimum(:auto_postpone_period) || Entropy::AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIODS_IN_SECONDS.min
cutoff = now - minimum_period + 1.second
candidate = base.where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", cutoff)
date_candidate_count = published.where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", cutoff).count
published_count = published.count
use_date_cursor = date_candidate_count * 10 < published_count
puts "mode=#{mode} cards=#{Card.count} due=#{base.count} date_candidates=#{date_candidate_count} published=#{published_count} selected=#{use_date_cursor ? 'range' : 'id'}"
puts "range_plan:"

puts "id_plan:"
puts connection.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN #{base.order(:id).limit(1001).to_sql}").map { |row| row["detail"] }
3.times do
  count = 0

    Card.uncached do
      date_candidate_count = published.where("cards.last_active_at <= ?", cutoff).count
      published_count = published.count
      if date_candidate_count * 10 < published_count
        candidate.find_each(batch_size: 1000, cursor: [ :last_active_at, :id ], order: [ :desc, :desc ]) { count += 1 }
      else
        base.find_each(batch_size: 1000) { count += 1 }
      end
    end
  end
  puts "adaptive_seconds=#{seconds.round(4)} loaded=#{count}"
  raise "selector mismatch" unless count == base.count
end
EOF

messages.content: I found a more selective approach that avoids global period estimates entirely: process each board using its effective board/account entropy period, and query that board’s cards with a `board_id,status,last_active_at,id` index. That makes each cutoff match the exact period for those cards and avoids count probes or races with other boards’ settings. I’ll compare this per-board query plan and runtime on the same 500,000-card fixtures before deciding whether to replace the adaptive implementation.

Entropy.insert_all!(board_ids.each_with_index.map { |id, i| { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: account_id, container_type: "Board", container_id: id, auto_postpone_period: periods[i], created_at: now, updated_at: now } })
board_sql = board_ids.map { |id| connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(id)) }
board_case = board_sql.each_with_index.map { |id, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{id}" }.join(" ")
period_case = periods.each_with_index.map { |period, i| "WHEN #{i} THEN #{period}" }.join(" ")
non_due_days = mode == "sparse" ? "((number % 2) + 1)" : "((number % 60) + 1)"
connection.execute(<<~SQL)

  SELECT randomblob(16), #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(account_id))},

         #{connection.quote(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(creator_id))}, number, 'published',

  FROM sequence

  DATE_RANGE_SELECTIVITY_DENOMINATOR = 10

    end

        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")

        .where("cards.last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', "#{EFFECTIVE_AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIOD_SQL} * 0.75")}", now)

      now = Time.now
      minimum_period = Entropy.minimum(:auto_postpone_period) || Entropy::AUTO_POSTPONE_PERIODS_IN_SECONDS.min

      published_cards = published

        end
      end
